title: Your own limit
topic: Cap your repayments with your bank data

steps.title: “Instalments: max 20% of my pay. The card bill: always in full.”
steps.body: Rules like these don't stop you buying things. They keep your [[committed-income]] small enough that one bad month doesn't roll into the next. Your rules, not a recipe.

steps.prompt: You earn €2,000. Your rule is “max 20% in instalments”. How much can you commit each month?
steps.explanation: 20% of €2,000 is €400. The four instalments from mission 2 were €420, so the rule would have said no to the last one.

steps.prompt: Why does “always pay the card bill in full” matter more than the exact limit?
options: Rolled-over card debt is usually the most expensive credit there is
Because the card stops working otherwise
Because paying in full earns interest
steps.explanation: [[revolving-credit]] grows on top of itself. Paying in full keeps the card a payment tool, not a loan.
